verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Pali dyeing and processing units with captive effluent treatment and verified order books; avoid units dependent on job-work for the Balotra and Jodhpur cluster, which is currently shut.
title: Pali textile dyeing & processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A dyeing and processing house takes grey fabric, water, power, dyes and chemicals, and returns finished dyed fabric on job-work or own-account terms. **Cash is made on throughput per day and on the spread between chemical and power cost and the processing rate, not on the fabric itself.** The value sits in the effluent treatment plant, boiler and continuous-processing line; the cash sits in receivables from fabric traders and powerloom owners. Working capital is inventory-heavy and receivable-driven, and ICRA's fabric methodology flags the sector as both fixed-capital and working-capital intensive [8][9]. So when a proposal lands, check the ETP capacity and consent-to-operate first; if the unit runs on a shared or hired ETP, ask who owns the consent and what happens if it lapses.

## What has broken now
**Processing units in Pali, Balotra and Jodhpur are shut, and the closure has already forced powerloom shutdowns downstream in Malegaon** [1][3]. That is local news, dated October 2026, and it is the single fact that governs this note. Rajasthan's own numbers confirm the stress: GST collections are -4.7% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, and electricity demand is +4.0% against India's +9.5% [D]. **The data pack scores this cluster at 50, a caution band, and the local news is worse than that score assumes.** India-wide IIP for NIC 13 is +13.1% YoY and +11.9% Apr-to-date [D], so the national textile output signal is healthy while Pali's local signal is not; do not let the national number pull a Pali proposal over the line.

## Where the growth is
**Pursue the units that are still running and picking up the order book the shut Balotra and Jodhpur units have dropped.** That means integrated processors with their own ETP and boiler, units with a confirmed buyer base in uniform and industrial fabric, and units adding capacity to absorb diverted job-work. Peer results support the demand side: Arvind's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23% to Rs 2,919 crore with net profit up 44% to Rs 148 crore [6], and Sportking's operating margin moved to 19% in Q1 FY27 from 12% a year earlier [7]. **Avoid pure job-work processors with no captive ETP, units whose order book is concentrated in the shut clusters, and any proposal where the promoter cannot show a consent to operate.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the fixed assets.** Take the ETP and plant as primary security, a charge on receivables, and a promoter guarantee. Set a drawing-power cap tied to verified receivables, and covenant a minimum ETP uptime and a maximum receivable days figure. **Every month take the GST return, the electricity bill, the ETP log and the receivable ageing.** The GST return is the cleanest local check because Rajasthan's collections are already running -4.7% [D]; a unit whose own GST outflow is falling while it reports rising sales is the first sign of trouble.

## Early-warning signs
- **Power consumption per metre of output falling while sales are reported rising** — check the CEA-linked state demand trend, which is +4.0% against India's +9.5% [D]; if a unit's own consumption diverges from that, ask for the meter reading.
- **Receivable days stretching past the sanctioned cycle** — ask for the buyer-wise ageing and stop fresh disbursement until it is explained.
- **Any notice or lapse on the consent to operate or ETP** — treat as a stop signal, given the cluster closures [1][3].
- **Job-work orders shifting to units in the shut clusters** — ask which buyers and which locations, and reprice the limit.
